scores.reason: Single-paper citation-grounded QA benchmark that explicitly rewards grounded refusal (Q4/C4), reports cross-model citation accuracy (C5), and shows citation metrics discriminate where LLM-judge scores don't — directly moves the measurement question.

Shows the unsupported-citation rate itself swings 3-18% with verifier choice — directly undermines what grounding numbers can legitimately support (C3) and supplies a calibrated bound (C4); exactly the premise-challenging measurement work the brief reaches for.

Expert-annotated benchmark of authentic claims with construction that avoids LLM-fabricated refutations (C3), accuracy broken down by evidence modality across 11 models (C1, C5), exposing figures as a specific failure mode.

Biomedical claim verification with rigorous evaluation showing retrieval benefit is source-dependent (C5) and evidence generation quality varies by system; relevant, though it leans toward health fact-checking rather than extraction from full papers.

Mechanistic probing that explains the known table-vs-chart verification gap as a routing failure; genuinely changes what fix to test next (research purpose), though it measures no extraction accuracy itself and covers only one error class.

Perspective paper arguing abstract-level benchmarks understate full-paper difficulty — directly relevant to what benchmark numbers can support (C3) and the brief's premise-challenging ask, but mostly gap-naming with only preliminary experiments.

Expert-annotated multimodal verification benchmark over 1,113 real papers, 21 models, reasoning-type breakdown and human error evaluation — squarely satisfies C1, C3 and C5 on the exact task the brief studies.

CLAIM-BENCH directly measures claim-evidence extraction and linking accuracy across six models (C1, C2, C5) on full-length papers, with a concrete closed/open model gap and prompting cost-accuracy tradeoff.

Foundational slot: ALCE is the canonical automatic citation-evaluation benchmark that later citation-faithfulness work in this list measures against; a newcomer skipping it would misread the verifier-reliability papers.

Foundational slot: WiCE established sub-claim decomposition and minimal-evidence entailment, real background for over-generalisation errors, but it is Wikipedia-domain and SciFact (named in the brief) is the more canonical anchor for scientific claim verification.
